title: Prefetch + KV-cache interaction: quant kernels probe notes
body:
Summary:

Working notes from an exploratory probe into an unusual tail-latency mode we observed during mixed-precision runs where KV-prefetch behavior appears to interact with quantization kernels (INT8/AWQ/FP8) and cause transient stalls / kernel oscillation on GPU. This doc records test harnesses, traces, hypotheses, short results, and recommended mitigations to validate in followups. Intended audience: runtime engineers, kernel team, and perf SREs.

Motivation / symptom:
- Customer-facing production incident (INF-3129) surfaced intermittent p99 spikes when serving long-context chat (avg seq 1k, bursty prefixes).
- Spikes correlate with quantized model variants (INT8 and AWQ) and happen more frequently on H100 pools with NVLink topology that mixes prefetch+async-kernel paths.
- Not reproduced deterministically in unit microbench; appears under realistic multiplexed traffic.

Experiments run (short):
1) Traffic replay: 10-minute replay of production trace (prefix-heavy) against single H100 (4-gpu node) with model variant: llama-like 13B in GPTQ vs AWQ vs native FP16.
   - client harness: tools/bench/replay_prefix.py --trace traces/long_prefix_june.json --rps 120 --concurrency 32 --seq-dist heavy-tail
2) Microtrace collection: NVIDIA nsight systems (nsys) and NVTX markers injected around prefetch, kv-lookup, kernel-launch, and kernel-complete.
3) Kernel sampling: collected per-kernel runtimes via runtime-instrumentation + per-kernel counters (cuda events).
4) Memory probes: host<->gpu memcpy times, PCIe vs NVLink ops, page-fault counts, and device free memory timeline.
5) Controlled perturbation: toggled prefetch on/off, capped prefetch window, and serialized prefetch requests.

Key observations:
- When prefetch is enabled with a large lookahead (prefetch N=32 cache entries), we see periodic 10–50ms stalls where the active compute kernel launch is delayed after memcpy completes.
- Stall windows align with spikes in host-to-device memcpy queue length and synchronous memory fences triggered by kernel variants that use larger shared scratch (observed with AWQ kernels that pack activations).
- INT8 kernels built on packed-matmul path show more frequent short stalls (~12ms) whereas FP8 (tensorcore-focused) shows fewer but longer tail events (~30–50ms) when they occur.
- GPTQ path (reference kernel) had the least jitter in our tests but at higher steady p50 latency compared to AWQ.
- Staggering prefetch (randomized offset) reduces correlation of stall windows with request arrival spikes, lowering p99 by ~18% in replay run.

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Prefetch-induced memcpy bursts are creating transient DMA saturation on NVLink/PCIe leading to kernel scheduling backpressure in driver -> delayed kernel dispatch.
2) Certain quant kernels (AWQ packing) allocate temporary device scratch that forces implicit global synchronizations or heavy L2 thrash causing subsequent kernel launches to wait for completion of housekeeping ops.
3) Host-side prefetch thread scheduling interacts with CUDA stream concurrency policies: when prefetch threads block or yield, they hold locks that serialize submission of small kernels.

Evidence pro/con: 
- Pro: nvprof traces show contiguous H2D memcpy bursts preceding stalls; GTF counters spike.
- Pro: Turning off packing in AWQ path (fallback to unpacked matmul) removes the long tail but increases cost (tokens/sec -9%).
- Con: Not all stalls line up with high H2D bandwidth; some align with increased device memory pressure indicating internal allocator churn.

Immediate mitigations tested (results):
- Bounded prefetch window (N<=8): reduces p99 by 12% with negligible throughput loss for typical workloads.
- Prefetch rate limiter: token-bucket rate limit on host prefetch threads reduced H2D spikes but added 2–3ms steady p50 due to throttling. Net p99 improvement positive.
- Prefer small-seq fastpath kernel when KV hit: added conditional path that avoids packing on low-latency hits — cut p95 by 9% at cost of +6% CPU work.

Instrumentation notes (how to reproduce probes):
- replay harness: tools/bench/replay_prefix.py --config experiments/kv-prefetch/config.yaml 
- nsys capture flags: nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=0 --output capture_prefetch
- NVTX annotations: mark prefetch_start / prefetch_end / kv_lookup / kernel_launch / kernel_complete around code paths.
- Collect cudaEvent timestamps for each kernel in service loop and emit to /tmp/kv-prefetch-timestamps.{pid}.log

Representative logs excerpt (abridged):
[2026-07-22T14:23:12.341Z] prefetch_start req=abcd prefix_len=512 prefetch_n=32
[2026-07-22T14:23:12.372Z] h2d_start bytes=1.2MB
[2026-07-22T14:23:12.389Z] h2d_end bytes=1.2MB
[2026-07-22T14:23:12.402Z] kernel_launch id=matmul_awq_stream_3
[2026-07-22T14:23:12.416Z] kernel_delayed id=matmul_awq_stream_3 delay_ms=17 reason=cuda-submit-wait

Quant-specific notes:
- AWQ packing reduces memory footprint but introduces an extra packing kernel which sometimes runs on the same stream used by compute; when packing is large it holds stream and causes compute to enqueue late.
- INT8 path uses custom packing + qweight layout; packing kernel is smaller but more numerous, causing many short stalls (many small delays rather than few large ones).
- FP8 path leverages fused tensorcore kernels and tends to be more 'atomic' (fewer separate kernels) so when it stalls it's because of larger contiguous work.

Proposed runtime heuristics (short list):
1) Adaptive prefetch budget: reduce prefetch N when observed inflight H2D ops > threshold or device_free_memory low.
2) Separate streams for packing vs compute with explicit stream priorities where hardware supports it (H100 stream priority API).
3) Prefetch jittering: randomized start offsets to avoid lockstep bursts across concurrent requests.
4) Prefetch backoff on allocator churn: if allocator stalls observed, pause prefetch for X ms.
5) Kernel packing budget per-GPU: limit concurrent packing kernels to M to prevent L2 thrash.
6) Trace-driven rollout: enable heuristics behind a rollout flag + per-model SLO gating.

Follow-ups / experiments to run next:
- Run same replay with NVLink disabled (force PCIe) to check bandwidth path sensitivity.
- Microbench to isolate allocator churn: stress test device malloc/free with packing sizes observed.
- Evaluate stream-priority changes on A100 vs H100 (different priority semantics).
- Reproduce with a different model architecture (MPT-30B) to see how attention head layout changes packing behavior.
- Implement an in-proc prefetch rate estimator based on recent H2D latency and try PID-style controller.

Open questions / risks:
- Will heuristics generalize to multi-tenant nodes with mixed-load types (embedding + generation)? Need cluster-level simulation.
- Packing fallback increases CPU cost and may worsen cost per token; need cost/perf tradeoff dashboard.
- Possible interactions with nvlink topologies and MIG (if enabled) unknown.

Action items (owners):
- Implement bounded prefetch flag and rollout to beta cluster (Aisha) — ETA: 2w.
- Kernel team to prototype separate packing stream and test priority semantics (Marco) — ETA: 3w.
- SRE to create replay job targeted at multi-tenant mix and run overnight (Daniela) — ETA: 1w.
- Bench team to evaluate cost impact of fastpath packing fallback across 3 workloads (Ethan) — ETA: 2w.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Consider a tiny on-device prefetch queue that is drained by a low-priority stream to decouple host submission bursts.
- Investigate whether cudaMemPrefetchAsync semantics combined with Unified Memory could yield smoother H2D pacing in some topologies.
- Short-term: expose prefetch window and packing fallback as feature flags in runtime config so we can A/B quickly.

Appendix: short perf numbers (replay run, single H100, 120rps, concurrency 32)
- FP16 baseline: p50 21.4ms, p95 45.8ms, p99 86.3ms, tps 420
- AWQ default (prefetch N=32): p50 18.9ms, p95 69.2ms, p99 178.4ms, tps 465
- AWQ bounded prefetch N=8: p50 19.7ms, p95 55.8ms, p99 146.8ms, tps 455
- INT8 default (prefetch N=32): p50 20.5ms, p95 60.3ms, p99 132.1ms, tps 452
- AWQ + staggered prefetch: p50 19.4ms, p95 53.9ms, p99 146.0ms, tps 460

If you're reading this: please add any local reproductions or alternate traces to linked_artifacts and tag runs with kv-prefetch in the experiment name.

-- Aisha
